title: Results, Figures and Tables: What Did They Find?
objective: Students learn to read data displays and explain results in clear academic English.
context: Classroom data: Students counted butterflies for ten minutes per site. Park = 15 butterflies. Garden = 10 butterflies. Field = 5 butterflies. They visited each site once.

items.prompt: What did the students measure? Give the unit and the time for each site.
items.answer: Number of butterflies seen at each site; butterflies per ten-minute observation.
items.hint: Look for the animal, the number, and the time.

items.prompt: Compare the highest and lowest sites. Use both counts and give the difference.
items.answer: Park 15, field 5. The park count was ten higher.
items.hint: Subtract the smaller number from the larger one.

items.prompt: A student says the highest site always has the most animals. What can you say from these data?
items.answer: The park had the highest count on this visit. One visit cannot show what always happens.
items.hint: Use: On this visit ... . We would need ... .
